catalog_quote: Moreover, in this case, the stress pattern of Taeq language generally falls on the penultimate syllable of a word, but the stress moves on to a long vowel when it occurs, for instance, the word Jonga (deer), Lalan (road), tEallo (today), lOlang (walk), bUlawang (gold), mawArang (thirsty), karAtasa (research), and kamawAtaKan (power). As seen those words above, the stress is made up from the long vowel and the stress falls penultimate syllable whether the word that has two, three, and four syllables. It also occurs at the level of the word that has affixes. The stress falls on the penultimate syllable like the word kamawAtaKan (power). Those examples can be concluded that the rule of stress patterns of Taeq language are determined by the stress falls on penultimate syllable of the word itself.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (10 pp., ABBYY text layer; Sawerigading 18(3), Dec 2012, open-access Balai Bahasa OJS; present and lists file->citation->URL for all six saved PDFs). Locator verified: PDF p. 5 = printed p. 355, left column, section '2.2. Taeq Language Stress Patterns'. I extracted the text layer (extracted text) and also rendered the page image at 110 and 250 dpi and read it directly: the quoted passage is there word for word ('Moreover, in this case, the stress pattern of Taeq language generally falls on the penultimate syllable of a word, but the stress moves on to a long vowel when it occurs, for instance, the word Jonga (deer), Lalan (road), tEallo (today), lOlang (walk), bUlawang (gold),…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Tae' (Taeq) falls on the penultimate syllable of the word, in di-, tri- and quadrisyllables and in affixed words alike; the author adds that stress is attracted to a long vowel where one occurs.
new_statements.exceptions: Stress 'moves on to a long vowel when it occurs' (the capitalised example vowels, e.g. bUlawang, karAtasa, kamawAtaKan, are not all penultimate, which the author attributes to vowel length); a confusing aside (p. 355 right column) says that in an affixed word like kamawa'takan the stressed [ta] can be 'word-final', 'only.. to the word that has with affix'. No systematic exception classes given.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, citation forms (isolated words listed as examples); statement is impressionistic background in an L2-English stress-transfer study by a Balai Bahasa linguist who works on Tae'; she states no prior research on Taeq stress existed and frames it against van Zanten, Stoel & Remijsen 2010 (penultimate stress prevailing in Sulawesi). Consistent with Grimes & Grimes 1987:94 (South Sulawesi languages usually penultimate; Toala'/Rongkong wordlists unmarked).
new_statements.identity_note: Garing 2012 writes the language name as 'Taeq' (= Tae', final glottal stop spelled q); her speakers are from Palopo/Luwu (Tae' proper, taee1237). Suparman 2022 describes the Rongkong dialect (Glottolog lists Rongkong as a Tae' dialect). Grimes & Grimes 1987 list the same speech varieties as two languages, Toala' (alt. Luwu, Toraja Timur, Sada, Toware') and Rongkong, in the Toraja-Sa'dan subfamily; their penultimate-stress remark (p. 94) is family-level, not Tae'-specific. Not to be confused with the Luwu dialect of Bugis (BLW in Grimes & Grimes).

sources.note: Sec. 2.2 'Taeq Language Stress Patterns' (p. 355): Taeq stress generally falls on the penultimate syllable of the word (2-, 3-, 4-syllable words, also affixed words), but 'moves on to a long vowel when it occurs'; examples Jonga, Lalan, tEallo, lOlang, bUlawang, mawArang, karAtasa, kamawAtaKan; author notes no prior research on Taeq stress and leans on van Zanten et al. 2010 (penultimate prevailing in Sulawesi).

sources.note: p. 94 (wordlist conventions): 'Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates from the normal pattern.. it is marked with an apostrophe.' Family-level statement; Tae' appears as Toala' and Rongkong (Toraja-Sa'dan subfamily); only Selayar is singled out for deviant (antepenultimate) stress.
